en: He leaves [?] awakened,
Their swords clashing,
Their heroes grapple with one another.
Heroes skilled in vengeance,
From the eagle poised over the small bird,
If they rush in, fighting,
If they meet in battle, they clash,
They sit around on the ground,
The man who made the sound,
He is pressed down to the ground,
Rejoicing when goodness is mentioned,
Grieving when a gentle song is mentioned,
The wrestlers in a single row,
Separating and enclosing them,
They watch the enemy’s side,
A man without strength,
Making him strike the tent,
Growing fierce, they match one another,
Driving them from place to place,
Breaking loose and falling, dark-eyed,
A blue cap broad as the place of honor,
Chermat’s appearance was like a mullah’s.
His bearing was exceptional,
Broad-chested, with a wide blaze,
Iron wound around the spear,
Its underside burning in the flame,
Standing properly prepared,
Mounted with flowing majesty,
Beyond lay Khiva and brave Afghan,
None fought more fiercely than he,
They encountered the oak-like champion,
Exhausted, they struck one another,
His back sweated upon the mountain pass,
From seeing what he had given,
None who came forth as an equal could match him,
At his side, the dark-eyed one,
Razym had a beard and a fur cap,
There is a most worthy man,
Ebedey and Kozoy were heroes
Their speech seemed heavenly
Kozoy of Beyish looked on
They crossed their spears
Their wolf-like tongues joined in challenge
Kozoy led the way
Ebedey stood and grappled
They drove through and broke the enemy
Driven by a devilish command
Against hero Ebedey
Mounting him amid shouts
A generous noble equal to all
Explaining his hardship
Defending his people and land
He trembled when taking up the fight
His eyes gleamed like Khydyr’s
The chief champion on the left
Many men stood on the right
He readied his spear
Saying the enemy had seen his sword
His frame seemed caught in battle
His heart sank then rose
Saying, understand like a tiny soul
There was no equal on earth to face him
Let him thrust his sword into the multitude
Fear the warrior’s courage
The brave one who suddenly engaged
His great age proved true
Saying his heart sank then rose
May he be a creature of many forms
When hero Kozoy took two
Ebedey who bore the banner
Taking on a beast-like form
Appearing like a standing hero
Beside every child
Toward the people on the flank
To draw what hung at his waist
To strike when advancing
When he came eastward
To grapple with Uzunkan
Settling into a beast-like form
Its head distinct, its shaft sharp
A great-headed mace was fastened
When given a shot, they pressed together
Fire came from its mouth
Blood came upon the messenger
A ridge rose where he stepped
An unforeseen quarrel arose
His abundance was by the thousand
His long neck stretched a fathom
His brow was a shield and amulet
His eyes were open and keen
To the Kazakhs, Kok Kaska was a plane tree
Among beasts he stood apart
He would besiege Talas and attack
He would seize it by force
The heroes Ebedey and Kozoy
Janaly and Karak, two khans
In the face of this enemy
The turmoil cast upon the people
Now he understood and became a hero
He became equal to the enemy ranks
His elder went far away
The hero struck in the great battlefield
Two saints came to his aid
The enemy raided and marched
They cast the enemy into that water
He bore an evil name on his lips
From Kayrat, who went at the head
Saying Ebedey and Kozoy were coming
The hero lamented over the war
He struck from behind and defended
A warrior was in our hands
When he was about to speak again
Seeing all the people as one
Saying, there is no warrior but me
Saying, none can stand as my equal
Saying, rise against the many Chinese
Calling him a self-stirred hero
One who learned by questioning the age
One who buried the dead
One who settled people from afar
Brave Kenen’s reach was far
He enriched those who camped on the summer pasture
He watched over a people who had suffered
He crossed waters at half flood
He grew among jagged middle mountains
His gaze grew fierce as a dragon’s
Of the white-capped Kyrgyz
Saying they fled toward the border
Trust it and contest the matter
Saying, hold firm and see
A spectacle fit to draw blood occurred
Facing the Kyrgyz in combat
Saying, let us attack in that way
So it was said from then on
They fell into just such a quarrel
Hearing news from those who went
Hero Kokjal took the lead
The black Kokjal drew blood
Those men went on
He became a blazing ember among the people
Hearing he was Seytek
There was nothing to say against him
None could overthrow him in counsel
No waist was strong enough to bear the sword
No heart had courage enough
Toward the ridges of Ala-Too
Your hero went straight ahead
There was none like him before
Saying the Kyrgyz remained here
Two raging heroes with Kozoy
Within a single burst of courage
The raging enemy gathered
They went like a whirlwind
He brought down his true sword
The enemy raged to the border
Their strength collapsed like sand
Sharpening his tongue against his foes,
Was he not one to speak it aloud?
What a discovery for every Nogoy,
A noble fellow skilled in marvels,
The incomparable hero Joltoy,
As though wading into dusky water.
Akjoltoy, alert as the wind,
Took up the blue-black powder.
He recited many a prayer by lamplight,
And the whole night had passed into light.
With neither mountain beast nor wolf nearby.
There was no person driving him onward,
Yet when released he does not cry out.
On this day he brooded inwardly,
Leaving no measure of unease behind,
This maddened creature before all living souls—
Put him at tether and he will not graze,
Tie him fast and he droops away.
After Kulunsur had shown this sign,
My dear, Kulunsur’s appearance has changed,
Though no news has arrived at all.
From a place devoid of tidings he gave one sign,
My dear, may no enemy be approaching.
His coat is ruffled and his aspect altered,
Kulunsur’s condition has turned ill.
Refusing the tether, he rolls upon the ground,
And frightens the livestock around him.
Such an appearance foretells grave trouble,
And news, if it comes, will bring an outcry.
This ill-omened swift horse,
Has no tongue to tell what drives him.
Kulbaran, the true enduring creature,
Neighs as if lamenting,
And pounds that very ground.
He capers and flaps his ears,
Beating and scattering the earth.
This sign that Kulunsur has given—
What event will it lead us into?
My heart says a grievous affair will come.
Seeing it, he called it a dreadful omen,
From the ill-fated racing steed.
He said that a warning had arrived.
Akjoltoy, seeing this,
Said, countless hosts, do not dismiss it.
From the gray-maned hero Seytek,
He paused and gave the matter heed.
Once Kulunsur had delivered the sign,
How could he stand without preparing?
There would be some remedy, noble fellow,
For this was a matter requiring broad wisdom.
He halted and girded his waist,
Then stood watching the mountain.
This noble creature Kulunsur,
Carried countless anxieties in distress.
In such unrest lay a dreadful calamity,
For there had been danger before.
This was no time for cutting work short,
He was a beast proven through hardship.
The steed streamed forward as though fully fed,
When urged, the racer met the mountain,
Galloping without restraint.
Hearing a cry, he would start in alarm,
When a moonless dark night fell.
He stumbled and grew fearful,
Yet after fleeing one day he would not slow.
Even when tied three times he endured,
Holding his water like a whetstone.
When every affair gripped the black earth,
And the snow held fast,
He was a beast as though winged.
Among animals he was the wisest,
Though the creature possessed no human tongue.
It was a mountain-like task for a man
Not a handful of Chymburak remained
Having exposed the truth to the enemy
Let a thousand youths test him
Even if they stand together
Enemies came from every side
Even then the warrior did not change expression
He would not tire even against a thousand
Come forth, even if a thousand of you arrive
If force is brought against his tiny life
Of the thousand at the edge
Truly he would not yield to the enemy
It was truly the battle’s very heat
He had an amulet
The coming dragon drove them
Joltoy would not leave it unconsidered
Joltoy the tiger-like warrior
Set the enemy apart from the living
Hero Seytek, the gray wolf
Descending with the eagle to hunt
Turning in haste and confusion
The enemy shouted again and again
A peak seemed to split in his hand
Making the whole world resound
Watching and knowing his defense
Of the black host and the multitude
Their shadows divided into countless parts
He struck them until they reeled
